title: SPIMA: Scalable and Cost-Efficient Sparse Matrix Multiplication via Processing in DRAM Array
problem: Sparse matrix multiplication faces irregular memory access patterns, bandwidth bottlenecks, and load imbalance on parallel architectures.
motivation: Processing-in-memory approaches can mitigate memory bandwidth bottleneck while maintaining scalability across varying sparsity patterns.
method: SPIMA leverages DRAM PIM with novel dataflow exploiting bank-level parallelism. Multiple input buffers, output buffer, and vector registers coordinate to enable data reuse even with high sparsity. Architecture co-designed for dataflow optimization.
key_novelty: PIM-based SpMM accelerator with dataflow maximizing input/output reuse and bank parallelism for highly sparse matrices.
contributions: Novel SpMM dataflow exploiting high DRAM bank-level parallelism
Architecture with multiple input buffers enabling efficient DRAM access scheduling
Robust performance across varying matrix sizes and sparsity patterns
Competitive performance vs. ASIC/FPGA accelerators on PIM-based systems

metrics.other: robust to matrix size and sparsity variations

limitations: Performance estimates rather than silicon results; scalability to very large sparse matrices (100M+) not demonstrated.
